q: When a capacitor is connected to a battery, the two conductors have charges of equal magnitude and ____ signs.
e: When a capacitor is connected to a battery, the two conductors have charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses.

q: The magnitude of the charge Q on each conductor is called the ____ of the capacitor.
e: The magnitude of the charge Q on each conductor is called the charge of the capacitor. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. The plates must conduct so charge can spread; the gap must insulate or the field collapses.

q: The potential difference between two conductors of the capacitor is called the potential ____ of the capacitor.
e: The potential difference between two conductors of the capacitor is called the potential difference of the capacitor. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The quantity of charge Q on the capacitor is linearly ____ to the potential difference V between the conductors.
e: The quantity of charge Q on the capacitor is linearly proportional to the potential difference V between the conductors. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential ____ of the capacitor.
e: The capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the ratio of the charge to the potential difference of the capacitor. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: The capacitance is represented by the equation C=____.
e: The capacitance is represented by the equation C=Q/V. The relation in this line is C=____. A nearby word in place of Q/V would name a different quantity.

q: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is the ____.
e: In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is the farad. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. In the SI system, the unit of capacitance is the ____. farad.

q: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is ____ F.
e: If the potential difference of the capacitor is 1V when it is given a charge 1 C, its capacitance is 1 F. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: The unit farad is named in honor of Michael ____.
e: The unit farad is named in honor of Michael Faraday. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

q: The farad is a very ____ unit of capacitance.
e: The farad is a very large unit of capacitance. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. The farad is a very ____ unit of capacitance. large.

q: In practice, typical devices have capacitances ranging from microfarad ($\mu F$) to ____.
e: In practice, typical devices have capacitances ranging from microfarad (µ F) to picofarad. A microfarad is 10^-6 F, the usual electrolytic size. A picofarad is 10^-12 F, the small ceramic and stray-capacitance scale.
1 microfarad (µ F) = 10^-6 F. A microfarad is 10^-6 F, the usual electrolytic size. The power 10^-6 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.
1 nanofarad (nF) = 10^-9 F. A nanofarad is 10^-9 F, a thousand times smaller than a microfarad. The power 10^-9 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.
1 picofarad (pF) = 10^-12 F. A picofarad is 10^-12 F, the small ceramic and stray-capacitance scale. The power 10^-12 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.

q: When the charge on the capacitor is increased, the potential difference also increases ____.
e: When the charge on the capacitor is increased, the potential difference also increases proportionally. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: When the charge on a capacitor is increased, its capacitance remains ____.
e: When the charge on a capacitor is increased, its capacitance remains constant. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Although the capacitance does not depend on Q and V, it depends on the size, shape, and the nature of the ____ between the two conductors.
e: Although the capacitance does not depend on Q and V, it depends on the size, shape, and the nature of the insulator between the two conductors. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the electric ____ of the conductor.
e: The amount of charge given to a conductor to change its potential by one unit is called the electric capacity of the conductor. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.
